newsitem.title: USA: R-P Rorer shrs off as Centeon woes linger.
newsitem.headline: R-P Rorer shrs off as Centeon woes linger.

text.p: Shares in Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc tumbled Monday as the company forecast earnings for 1997 which were below consensus estimates, partly due to lingering costs associated with a product recall, analysts said.

The company, the pharmaceuticals unit of Rhone-Poulenc SA, earlier reported 1996 earnings of $3.16 per share in 1996 compared to $2.53 per share in 1995 and a First Call mean estimate of $3.36 per share.

Rhone-Poulenc Rorer said earnings in 1996 would have been higher were it not for a recall of an albumin product at its Centeon LLC joint venture with Hoechst AG. The company announced the recall in October, as a precaution against risk of bacterial infection.
Costs associated with the recall hurt the year $0.44 per share, it said.

In an interview with Reuters, Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Chief Financial Officer Patrick Langlois said the company's earnings would grow 15 to 20 percent in 1997 from a base of $3.16 per share, a forecast which he said included any possible future impact from the recall.
But this was below the First Call mean estimate of $4.01 per share for 1997, analysts said, adding that many were forced to lower estimates.
Steven Gerber, an analyst at Oppenheimer & Co, said he lowered his 1997 earnings estimate to $3.75 per share from $4.05 per share and his 1998 estimate to $4.50 per share from $4.60 per share.
"Shares are down due to the lagging impact of a big product recall at Centeon into the first quarter and a very severe impact from health reform measures in France," he said.

Langlois also said the company would not ship the albumin product in the first quarter 1997, due to the lag time between production and shipment. The company resumed production of the drug in late January, it said.
"There are also a lot of uncertainties regarding the product and its market share position," Langlois said.
Analysts echoed this statement, saying it usually took time for a recalled product to regain market share once it returned to the shelves.
Rhone-Poulenc Rorer shares traded off 4-1/2 at 71-1/2 by 1557 EST/2057 GMT.
"This isn't a one-time accounting charge," another analyst said. "Centeon is part of the company's business, it is part of what they do."
